topicsSubtitle: Hierarchical view of the current OpenAlex Topics taxonomy
conceptsSubtitle: Hierarchical view of the legacy OpenAlex Concepts taxonomy (superseded by Topics)
openAlexDesc: OpenAlex is a fully open catalog of the global research system, providing free access to hundreds of millions of scholarly works, authors, institutions, and more. It serves as an open alternative to proprietary services like Scopus and Web of Science.
topicsDesc: Topics are the current subject-classification system used by OpenAlex. Each Topic represents a relatively specific research theme and belongs to a Subfield, Field, and Domain, forming a fixed four-level taxonomy.
conceptsDesc: Concepts are OpenAlex's earlier scholarly concept system. It contains about 65,000 concepts connected through ancestor/parent relationships and spans up to roughly six levels. This taxonomy was later superseded by Topics, so this page is retained as a historical data view and should not be interpreted as the current Domain → Field → Subfield → Topic hierarchy.
topicFeature1: About 4,500 Topics across all research areas
topicFeature2: Current subject classification for OpenAlex works
conceptFeature2: Concept hierarchy based on ancestor/parent relationships
topicFeature3: Fixed four levels: Domain → Field → Subfield → Topic
conceptFeature3: Legacy system: 19 level-0 root concepts with descendants extending to about level 5
topicsTreeDesc: Topics are organized in OpenAlex's current fixed 4-level taxonomy:
conceptsTreeDesc: Legacy Concepts do not use the Domain → Field → Subfield → Topic taxonomy. They are organized by Concept level and ancestor/parent relationships, with about 65,000 concepts descending from 19 level-0 root concepts and reaching roughly level 5:
hierarchyConceptsLevel0: 🌐 Level 0 — Root concepts (19 top-level concepts, e.g. Computer Science, Medicine)
hierarchyConceptsLevel1: ↳ Level 1 — Broad child concepts under a level-0 root
howToUseDesc: Browse the hierarchy or search by name. The Topics page shows the current taxonomy, while the Concepts page is for exploring the historical Concepts taxonomy. Click the OpenAlex button on a node to view related content.
usageTip1: Click a node to expand and explore sub-categories
usageTip2: Use search to filter and highlight matching concepts
usageTip3: View works counts and child-node statistics
worksCountTitle: Total scholarly works in this category
